question: How do Django REST Framework permissions work and how do you write custom permissions?
title: DRF Permissions
direct_answer: Permissions are checked after authentication. Built-in: IsAuthenticated, IsAdminUser, AllowAny, IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly. Set globally in DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES or per-view with permission_classes. Custom permissions: subclass BasePermission, implement has_permission(request, view) for view-level and has_object_permission(request, view, obj) for object-level. Return False to deny (403). Raise PermissionDenied for custom error messages.
interviewer_intent: Tests DRF security knowledge — permissions are a core concept in every DRF API.

seo.metaTitle: DRF Permissions — IsAuthenticated, Custom BasePermission, Object-Level
seo.metaDescription: Django REST Framework permissions: built-in IsAuthenticated, custom BasePermission, has_object_permission for row-level access control.

speakable_v2.hook: DRF splits access control cleanly: authentication says who you are, permissions say what you can do.

beats.content: IsAuthenticated is the most common. IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly allows reads from anyone but restricts writes to authenticated users — good for public APIs.
Subclass BasePermission. has_permission for view-level (is the user allowed to access this endpoint?). has_object_permission for object-level (is the user allowed to access this specific record?).
Permission classes are ANDed together: all must pass. Use list [IsAuthenticated, IsOwnerOrReadOnly] for both authentication check and ownership check.

speakable_v2.cap: has_object_permission is only called if has_permission passes. Don't put all your logic in has_object_permission — it won't run for list views where individual objects aren't fetched.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with djangorestframework-guardian for database-backed object permissions, or DRF throttling for rate limiting.
